2607.05317.title: Shape Over Intensity: Directional Topological Encoding for False Positive Reduction in Intracranial Aneurysm Detection
2607.05317.paper_summary: Automated detection of intracranial aneurysms (IAs) from CT angiography (CTA) is severely hindered by high false-positive rates. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) rely on local pixel intensities, causing systematic confusion between saccular aneurysms and vascular bifurcations - a problem especially acute for small lesions (<3 mm), where detection sensitivity falls below 60%. We propose a plug-and-play, topology-aware false-positive reduction framework evaluating the Smooth Euler Characteristic Transform (SECT) - a directional representation encoding global 3D vascular geometry independently of intensity - against persistence-based summaries (Persistence Images and Landscapes), tested on a stratified subset of the RSNA 2025 dataset. SECT achieves an AUC of 0.943, substantially outperforming direction-agnostic methods (AUC ~0.68), and exhibits a clinical performance inversion: it excels on the sub-3 mm cohort, maintaining 0.943 AUC and 78.5% sensitivity at 95% specificity. The representation is also scanner-agnostic, achieving 0.927 mean AUC under leave-one-scanner-out (LOGO) validation across four manufacturers. By capturing asymmetric geometric invariants rather than intensity profiles, SECT reliably resolves the primary structural confounder in IA detection, positioning it as a robust downstream filter for hybrid deep-learning diagnostic pipelines.
2607.05317.paper_summary_zh: 自動檢測腦內動脈瘤（IAs）從CT血管造影（CTA）受到高假陽性率的嚴重阻礙。卷積神經網絡（CNNs）依賴於局部像素強度，導致囊狀動脈瘤與血管分叉之間的系統性混淆——這對於小病變（<3 mm）尤其明顯，檢測靈敏度低於60%。我們提出了一個即插即用的、考慮拓撲的假陽性減少框架，評估平滑歐拉特徵變換（SECT）——這是一種獨立於強度的方向性表示，編碼全球3D血管幾何，並與基於持續性的總結（持續圖像和地形圖）進行比較，該框架在RSNA 2025數據集的一個分層子集中進行測試。SECT達到了0.943的AUC，顯著優於無方向性的方法（AUC約為0.68），並顯示出臨床表現的逆轉：它在小於3 mm的隊列中表現卓越，維持0.943的AUC和在95%特異性下的78.5%靈敏度。該表示也與掃描儀無關，在四個製造商的留一掃描儀驗證（LOGO）中達到了0.927的平均AUC。通過捕捉不對稱幾何不變量而不是強度輪廓，SECT可靠地解決了IA檢測中的主要結構混淆因素，使其成為混合深度學習診斷管道的穩健下游過濾器。
2607.05317.author: Akshay Gokhale et.al.
